text:
gpui-kit-grid

 

A live GPUI data grid, for applications built with gpui-kit: a real-time table of hundreds of thousands of rows that takes thousands of updates per second from any thread, with change highlight and with sorting, filtering, grouping and trees in the background.

 

The quotes example: every change highlighted as it arrives, live totals per sector. Run it in the browser, where the examples are compiled to WebAssembly and drawn with WebGPU: the WebGPU demo page says how, and the trade blotter page has one to fill.

It is a separate crate on top of gpui-kit. Rows are addressed by key and written from any thread; a background ingest collapses updates by key and publishes snapshots; the order on screen is rebuilt in the background; one custom element paints the visible cells. The ideas come from the LiveGrid grid (WinForms), rethought for GPUI.

 Documentation: · Getting started · Examples · Live demos · API · crates.io

 Status: version 2 is on crates.io. Stages 1–3 are done: the live core, grouping, aggregates and trees, then editing, elements in cells, export and drag and drop. The API will still change, in major versions: one for each gpui-kit minor release the grid moves to. What may come next is in ROADMAP.md.

 Why a new grid when gpui-kit has DataTable

 DataTable builds an element for each visible cell, addresses rows by index and calls its delegate through &mut on the UI thread. That is enough for static tables, not for live data: with 1500 visible cells under 2k updates a second a frame takes 12–14 ms, and after a re-sort the selection points at a different row.

 DataTable gpui-kit-grid 
 --- --- --- 
 Painting An element per visible cell One custom element, glyphs painted directly 
 Frame, 1500 cells, 2k updates/s 12–14 ms 1.1 ms 
 Rows and selection By index By key: survive re-sorting and removal 
 Data &mut delegate on the UI thread GridWriter from any thread, background ingest 
 Sorting and filtering The delegate sorts on a click, on the UI thread; no filtering In the background, automatic when data changes 
 Change highlight No Yes, with direction arrows and fading removed rows 
 Structure Flat rows Grouping, aggregates, totals and trees, built in the background 
 Editing and export No editing; cells as text ( dump ), written out by the application Editors under live updates; copy as TSV, CSV and custom formats in the background 

Measured with the headless spike bench example (release, macOS); the Performance page has every scenario.

Rust data grids compared sets the grid beside the other GPUI tables and those of egui, iced, Slint, GTK and Dioxus.

 Install

 

Each major version of the grid is built against one minor release of gpui-kit, which pins its GPUI snapshot exactly:

 gpui-kit-grid gpui-kit Rust 
 --- --- --- 
 2 0.10 1.98 
 1.0 (GitHub only, tag v1.0.0 ) git revision 146ab45 1.95 

 decimal (exact money values) and derive ( [derive(GridColumns)] ) are off by default; Getting started walks through a first grid.

The window shows LiveGrid::new(&grid) , and the application calls gpui kit grid::init(cx) after gpui kit::init(cx) for the grid's keys. The whole program is crates/grid/examples/quickstart.rs ; Getting started walks through it, with installation.

 Examples

 Example What it shows 
 --- --- 
 quickstart The smallest application: 1000 trades from a producer thread 
 cookbook Recipes: a reload with progress, a held order, a saved layout, a custom export, a WebSocket feed 
 blotter Every feature of stages 1 and 2 on a trade blotter: grouping, totals, change arrows, a held order, a status bar on LiveGridHandle 
 portfolio A live tree of funds, desks, books and positions 
 dock layout Grids in a dock, with layouts saved and restored 
 orders Orders edited in place under live updates: every editor, elements in cells, CSV export, drag and drop 
 desk , ladder , wire , broker Trading screens over a simulated market 
 ops A data-centre console in a simulated alert storm 
 orbit About 17,000 satellites from CelesTrak's public data 
 transit Munich by the timetable, and Helsinki live 
 wiki Wikimedia's live edits, a row per wiki 
 ships Every vessel around Finland, live from AIS 
 perf This machine's processes and GPU, live (macOS and Linux) 
 spike bench The headless benchmark (macOS) 

Run one with cargo run --release -p gpui-kit-grid --example ( spike bench also needs --features test-support ). Each example lists its environment variables at the top of its main.rs . The showcase examples' fonts are downloaded with python3 -I script/fetch-example-fonts , and orbit 's and transit 's data with script/fetch-orbit-data and script/fetch-transit-data . desk , broker , ops , orbit , transit , wiki and ships also run in the browser, with a quotes page beside them ( crates/grid-web ; see Web).

 Documentation

- Concepts: rows by key, ingest and snapshots, background rebuilds, and what the grid is for.
- Replaceable behaviors: every default is a strategy you can replace.
- Guides: grouping, tree, live changes, cells, editing, export, drag and drop, columns, keyboard, settings.
- Cookbook, Performance, Web, Embedding.

The site is built from site/ (Astro Starlight): bun install --cwd site --frozen-lockfile , then bun run --cwd site build and bun test --cwd site . Code on its pages comes from // region blocks of compiled files, and bun test checks that this README's snippets match them. The site also ships as a container image, ghcr.io/giglabocom/gpui-kit-grid-site (nginx, docker/site/ ), released on its own tags; see "Releases" in CONTRIBUTING.md.

 Development
